title: Raymond Burr
wiki_lead:
Raymond William Stacy Burr (May 21, 1917 – September 12, 1993) was a Canadian actor who had a lengthy Hollywood film career and portrayed the title roles in the television dramas Perry Mason and Ironside.
Burr's early acting career included roles on Broadway, radio, television, and film, usually as the villain. He portrayed the suspected murderer in the Alfred Hitchcock thriller Rear Window (1954), and he also had a role in the 1956 film Godzilla, King of the Monsters!, which he reprised in the 1985 film Godzilla 1985. He won Emmy Awards for acting in 1959 and 1961 for the role of Perry Mason, which he played for nine seasons (1957–1966) and reprised in a series of 26 Perry Mason TV movies (1985–1993). His second TV series, Ironside, earned him six Emmy and two Golden Globe nominations.
Burr died from liver cancer in 1993, and his personal life came into question, as many details of his biography appeared to be unverifiable.

Early life
Raymond William Stacy Burr was born May 21, 1917, in New Westminster, British Columbia. His father, William Johnston Burr (1889–1985), was a hardware salesman; his mother, Minerva Annette (née Smith, 1892–1974), was a pianist and music teacher.
When Burr was six, his parents divorced. He moved to Vallejo, California, with his mother and younger siblings Geraldine and James, while his father remained in New Westminster. Burr briefly attended San Rafael Military Academy in San Rafael, California, and graduated from Berkeley High School.
In 1986, he told journalist Jane Ardmore that, when he was 12 years old, his mother sent him to New Mexico for a year to work as a ranch hand.  According to Burr's story, he was already his full adult height and rather large and "had fallen in with a group of college-aged kids who didn't realize how young Raymond was, and they let him tag along with them in activities and situations far too sophisticated for him to handle." In the same article, Burr also stated he developed a passion for growing things and joined the Civilian Conservation Corps for a year in his teens. He made his stage debut at age 12 in a Vancouver stock company, and did some acting in his teens. The experiences Burr described when he was the age of 12 (working in radio in San Francisco, spending a year in New Mexico, appearing in Vancouver theatre, working for the Civilian Conservation Corps) are sometimes mutually contradictory; this would be a pattern that would recur in Burr's autobiographical reminiscences about his pre-Perry Mason personal life. 


Acting career


Theatre
Burr grew up during the Great Depression and hoped to study acting at the Pasadena Playhouse, but he was unable to afford the tuition. By his own account, in 1934 he joined a repertory theatre company in Toronto that toured throughout Canada, then joined another company that toured India, Australia, and England. grok_lead: Raymond Burr (May 21, 1917 â September 12, 1993) was a Canadian-American actor renowned for his iconic portrayals of defense attorney Perry Mason in the long-running television series Perry Mason (1957â1966) and wheelchair-bound detective Robert T. Ironside in Ironside (1967â1975), roles that established him as a staple of American television drama. Born Raymond William Stacy Burr in New Westminster, British Columbia, his parents separated when he was six, after which he moved with his mother to Vallejo, California. Burr's acting career began in earnest after a series of odd jobs during the Great Depression, including stints as a ranch hand, deputy sheriff, and nightclub singer; he later owned an art gallery on Rodeo Drive. He made his film debut in San Quentin (1946) and gained prominence in the 1950s playing menacing villains, most notably the voyeuristic killer Lars Thorwald in Alfred Hitchcock's Rear Window (1954). Transitioning to television, he starred in over 270 episodes of Perry Mason, earning two Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series in 1959 and 1961, and later received six Emmy nominations and two Golden Globe nominations for Ironside. He reprised the role of Perry Mason in 26 television movies from 1985 until his death, further cementing his legacy as the embodiment of the shrewd, ethical lawyer created by author Erle Stanley Gardner. In his personal life, Burr maintained a long-term partnership with actor Robert Benevides, with whom he co-founded Raymond Burr Vineyards in Sonoma County in 1986, producing its first bottling in 1989; he was also a dedicated philanthropist, sponsoring 26 foster children, establishing the American Fijian Foundation to support Pacific Island communities, and breeding over 1,500 new orchid varieties, many of which he donated to institutions like Cal Poly Pomona. Burr owned a private island in Fiji for orchid cultivation and was among the first in the U.S. to import and breed Portuguese Water Dogs. He developed deep ties to legal education, receiving an honorary Doctor of Laws degree from the University of the Pacific's McGeorge School of Law in 1960 and contributing significantly through fundraisers, donations of Perry Mason scripts, and advocacy support. Burr passed away from kidney cancer at his Northern California ranch at age 76, leaving a profound impact on television history and horticulture.
